pairs.question: Ergo iam ille bonus filius meus habet amicam aliquam? prome agedum, quae sola mihi servis amanter, nomen eius, quae puerum ingenuum et investem sollicitavit, sive illa de Nympharum populo seu de Horarum numero seu de Musarum choro vel de mearum Gratiarum ministerio.
pairs.answer: Nescio, domina: puto puellam--si probe memini, Psyches nomine dicitur--efflicte cupere.
pairs.derivation: Direct-speech exchange between Venus and the gull. Stripped the framing tag 'at Venus irata solidum exclamat repente:' before Venus's words and normalized the initial capital. Venus's whole speech is one demand-question (does Cupid have a girlfriend, and what is her name); kept it contiguous and verbatim. The bird's reply is stripped of the interleaved framing 'Nec loquax illa conticuit avis, sed ... inquit, ...' and 'domina:' retains its place; the answer runs to its single full stop ('efflicte cupere.') and genuinely answers by naming Psyche. The '--' marks are the edition's parenthetical dashes (not editorial angle brackets) and are kept.
